name: The Dominick
positioning: A 46-story glass tower on the corner of Spring and Varick Streets, between SoHo and Hudson Square, with Rockwell Group interiors and Fendi Casa furnishings
best_for: Travelers who want a downtown Manhattan base with floor-to-ceiling windows
Spa-goers drawn to a hammam, a salt chamber and a honey-based signature ritual
Guests traveling with a small dog

facts.text: The Dominick is a sleek glass tower that stands 46 stories tall.
The hotel is anchored by a quiet stretch of Dominick Street, which gives it its name.
The hotel sits on the corner of Spring and Varick Streets.
It sits between the cobblestone streets of SoHo and the creative energy of Hudson Square.
Guests can stroll to MacDougal Street's bars and comedy clubs, with easy access to Tribeca, Greenwich Village and the subway.
The hotel was designed by the Rockwell Group.
Inside, minimalist design meets warmth through natural materials and Fendi Casa furnishings.
Bathrooms are oversized, with standalone rain showers and a separate bath.
The Sisley Spa is on the seventh floor.
The spa offers a Moroccan hammam and an inhalation salt chamber.
The hotel keeps beehives on its roof in partnership with Bee Haven.

highlights.text: The spa's honeybee ritual is a 90-minute treatment with a full-body mask derived from the hotel's own harvested honeybees.
On the seventh-floor terrace, staff can book cabana suites, poolside lounge chairs and poolside massages.
One of the guestrooms is a penthouse turned into a gallery.
The duplex penthouse has its own terrace.
The hotel has spa suites with private saunas.

considerations.text: The rooftop pool closes for the season after Labor Day Weekend.
The hotel is dog-friendly only for dogs under 25 pounds.
WhataHotel notes the busy urban setting may not suit guests seeking tranquility.
